task.name: A preflight response that fails to parse is recorded as a founded classification, and the substituted values are cached and summarised as measured
task.story_text:
## Observed

Run `1a6b6e18d232` (story issue-2216, sprint `issues-2191,2216,2500,2475,2138`) recorded
a preflight classification that contradicts what the preflight agent actually produced.

The agent's response, recoverable only from the prose `reason` string left in
`.forge/audits/runs/1a6b6e18d232.json`, contained a complete and well-formed
classification:

    verdict: PROCEED
    complexity_score: 7
    complexity: medium
    work_type: bug
    domains: [parsing, backend]
    contract_change: false

The stored preflight block for that same run instead reads `complexity_score: 5`,
`domains: []`, `degraded: false`, and `complexity_source: preflight`. The `reason` field
records `"Failed to parse preflight YAML; falling back to PROCEED"`, so the parse is known
to have failed, yet nothing else in the record says the classification was not founded by
the classifier. `complexity_source` claims `preflight` provenance rather than
`preflight_degraded_conservative`, which is the label that exists to mark exactly this
case.

The damage did not stay inside the run. The preflight result was cached
(`cached: true`, `cache_validation.status: accepted`) and reused, so the substituted
classification became the cached answer for that story. The run's knowledge summary
`.forge/knowledge/summaries/1a6b6e18d232.yaml` inherited `domains: []` and is the only run
of six in that sprint with no domains, permanently missing a retrieval signal the prior-run
selector scores at weight 6 while every sibling summary carries two domains.

The cache entry names `source_run_id: e887dab00ac4`, and no run record by that id exists on
disk, so the origin of the cached value cannot be inspected to determine whether the
degraded flag was set at parse time and lost when the result was cached, or never set.

The story under preflight was issue-2216, whose own subject is field loss after a nested
code fence. The preflight extractor takes the text between the first fence marker and the
next one with no handling for fences appearing inside the extracted content, and the
agent's `reason` prose was quoting fenced material when the truncation occurred.

## Expected

A response that fails to parse must not be able to present itself as a founded
classification. When any part of a classifier's output is lost, the values the coordinator
substitutes are its own fallback rather than anything the classifier observed, and every
surface that reports them must say so — the provenance label, the degraded flag, and the
run record must agree with each other and with what actually happened, so that an operator
or a later automated reader cannot mistake a substituted value for a measured one. A single
prose sentence buried in a reason string is not that signal, because nothing downstream
reads it.

Degradation must also survive every path a classification can travel. A result that is
cached, restored, summarised, or copied into a durable corpus carries its degraded status
with it, so a value that was never founded cannot silently acquire the appearance of one by
being stored and read back. A cached classification whose originating record is no longer
available is itself a state the system must be able to report rather than one that leaves
the question unanswerable.

Where a parser recovers a structured response from surrounding text, content that resembles
a delimiter inside the response must not be able to truncate it. This applies wherever such
recovery happens, not only in the flow where it was most recently observed — a fix that
repairs one extractor and leaves its siblings with the same construction has not addressed
the category.

## Diagnosis

**Baseline:** `b891c03e6455295bea6f53ddcda4b926392f1d26` captured at `2026-08-19T15:13:31.843015+00:00`

**Inspected files:**

- `.forge/audits/runs/1a6b6e18d232.json` — `sha256:a21f6c75a43343550af4ac02ccae24fc85210466e226166c461c3aa8f49d6343`
- `.forge/knowledge/summaries/1a6b6e18d232.yaml` — `sha256:c731e854bd587a571e05331d14f0bc51e38d629fc9025b3a494f041d76f0887b`
- `src/theforge/coordinator/preflight.py` — `sha256:2b7772a9354c8bb374f77264b9e1aa99ef9e57e74083e26696be9b3b327c4353`
- `src/theforge/coordinator/preflight_flow.py` — `sha256:92d62d888fc2d23ae45fed1463e91de5360110689797d84f9aab8d1bd5519215`
- `src/theforge/coordinator/preflight_cache.py` — `sha256:0f6500322e943c305a022d7fc505d48b889dca67585138f8ddb8e038aaeb3559`
- `src/theforge/coordinator/state.py` — `sha256:2227d50293e3233a3de0861ace26eb8c2c22564a5197d5955a7a79c00a5eae7c`
- `src/theforge/coordinator/engine.py` — `sha256:240ee318cd69ec8f1f0d8ff492ba95c8cbbc0364d207a065c7f342b116cca158`
- `src/theforge/coordinator/resume_persistence.py` — `sha256:b54b70b8dd3e0ede16af082c927018571a995bbc72bc25cf7a878d6afc9e4d46`
- `src/theforge/sprint/runner.py` — `sha256:723a50777dec2f41a76aeb6a4c7430198f5be90f348c0263aa596c3c64dc2ec5`
- `tests/test_preflight_degraded_disclosure.py` — `sha256:f1f9ffebd14b2c56887336571e8b35f41805f8b60f73147ee70216348d85cdce`

### Observed symptom

A story that reuses a cached preflight verdict from a sibling run in the same
sprint can silently lose the fact that the original classification was
degraded (parse-failed). The reusing run's audit record reports
`degraded: false`, `degraded_reason: null`, and `complexity_source: preflight`
(i.e. "founded"), even when the cached values were themselves the fallback
substituted after a YAML parse failure. The degradation label does not
survive the copy from a cached in-memory preflight state onto a new run's
state, so a substituted value acquires the appearance of a measured one once
it is reused, and that mislabeled value then flows into the preflight cache
record and the run's knowledge summary.

### Reproduction / evidence

`.forge/audits/runs/1a6b6e18d232.json`: `preflight.cached: true`,
`preflight.cache_validation.status: accepted`,
`preflight.source_run_id: "e887dab00ac4"`, `preflight.degraded: false`,
`preflight.degraded_reason: null`, `preflight.complexity_source: preflight`,
while `preflight.reason` begins "Failed to parse preflight YAML; falling
back to PROCEED. Raw: ```yaml\nverdict: PROCEED\ncomplexity_score: 7\n...",
proving the classifier's real output was well-formed and only failed to
parse (the truncation matches issue #2216's nested-fence extraction bug),
yet the reused record carries no trace of that failure anywhere but the
prose `reason` string.

Root cause located directly in code:
`src/theforge/coordinator/preflight_cache.py:127-166`,
`apply_cached_preflight_state()`. This function copies every preflight
output field from `cached_state` (the in-memory `CoordinatorState` of the
sibling run that produced the cacheable verdict, held in
`preflight_states` for the duration of one `forge sprint` batch-preflight
pass — see `src/theforge/sprint/runner.py` `run_batch_preflight`) onto the
live `state` for the reusing story. It copies `preflight_verdict`,
`preflight_reason`, `preflight_complexity`, `preflight_complexity_score`,
`preflight_domains`, `preflight_work_type`, `preflight_contract_change`,
etc. — but never copies `preflight_degraded`, `preflight_degraded_reason`,
`preflight_failure_action`, `preflight_risk_signals`, or
`preflight_partial_evidence`. `CoordinatorState` (`state.py:715-733`)
defaults `preflight_degraded` to `False` and `preflight_degraded_reason` to
`None`, so the reusing run's freshly-constructed `state` simply keeps those
defaults regardless of what the source run actually recorded.

`complexity_source()` (`preflight.py:44-50`) and `degraded_preflight_fields()`
(`preflight.py:67-75`) both read `state.preflight_degraded` — since that
attribute was never overwritten by the cache copy, both correctly-written
functions compute `complexity_source: "preflight"` and `degraded: false`
from a state that never received the true value. The bug is the missing
copy, not the provenance-computation logic (which is otherwise correct, as
proven by the separate, disk-persisted resume-record restore path
`_apply_preflight()` in `resume_persistence.py:809-846`, which *does*
include `("preflight_degraded", "degraded")` and
`("preflight_degraded_reason", "degraded_reason")` in its restore list —
showing the project's own convention for how this field must be carried,
a convention `apply_cached_preflight_state()` does not follow).

This explains every downstream symptom named in the issue: the cache
snapshot written from this run's state (`cache_snapshot`/`cache_validation`
in the audit) inherits the un-flagged `degraded: false`, and
`.forge/knowledge/summaries/1a6b6e18d232.yaml`'s `story_shape` /
`domains: []` are generated from the same understated state.

### Hypotheses tested

- **[ruled out]** The preflight YAML parser (_parse_preflight_verdict et al. in preflight.py) fails to set degraded=True on a parse failure, so the flag is wrong from the moment of parsing.
  - Evidence: preflight.py:376-417 _parse_preflight_verdict returns degraded=True on any yaml.YAMLError or on a non-dict/invalid-verdict parse. preflight_flow.py:521-528 assigns state.preflight_degraded = True and state.preflight_degraded_reason = "parse_error" whenever _parse_preflight_verdict reports parse_degraded — this path is correct and is what the *originating* run e887dab00ac4 must have gone through, matching the surviving 'Failed to parse preflight YAML...' reason text.
- **[confirmed]** apply_cached_preflight_state() (preflight_cache.py) omits preflight_degraded/preflight_degraded_reason/preflight_failure_action/preflight_risk_signals from the field-by-field copy it performs from the source run's live CoordinatorState onto the reusing run's state, so the reusing state keeps its class defaults (False/None) no matter what the source run recorded.
  - Evidence: preflight_cache.py:127-166 copies ~18 preflight_* attributes (verdict, reason, complexity, complexity_score, domains, work_type, contract_change, bundle_candidate, batch_group, warnings, likely_files, result, duration_s, criteria_checked, cache_snapshot) but never touches preflight_degraded, preflight_degraded_reason, preflight_failure_action, preflight_risk_signals, or preflight_partial_evidence. state.py:715-733 defaults these to False/None/[]/None. The disk-persisted resume-record restore path (_apply_preflight in resume_persistence.py:809-846) explicitly includes ('preflight_degraded','degraded') and ('preflight_degraded_reason','degraded_reason') in its restore tuple list, confirming this is a known, deliberately-carried field elsewhere in the same subsystem — the cache-reuse path is simply missing it.
- **[ruled out]** The knowledge summary generator or the cache-write path re-derives degraded status independently and gets it wrong, rather than the state-copy step being the fault.
  - Evidence: complexity_source() and degraded_preflight_fields() in preflight.py:44-75 both derive their output purely from state.preflight_degraded — there is no separate re-derivation logic downstream. Once state.preflight_degraded is (wrongly) False after the cache copy, every consumer of that state (routing audit stamp, knowledge summary, cache snapshot) faithfully reports 'founded' because that is genuinely what the state says at that point.

### Confirmed cause

`apply_cached_preflight_state()` in `src/theforge/coordinator/preflight_cache.py`
(lines 127-166) copies a preflight verdict and its classification fields
from a cached sibling `CoordinatorState` onto a reusing story's fresh
`CoordinatorState`, but the copy list omits `preflight_degraded`,
`preflight_degraded_reason`, `preflight_failure_action`, and
`preflight_risk_signals`. Because `CoordinatorState` defaults these to
`False`/`None`/`[]`, a reusing run whose source classification was degraded
(e.g. by a YAML parse failure) ends up with an un-degraded state: every
downstream consumer that legitimately derives its output from
`state.preflight_degraded` — `complexity_source()`, `degraded_preflight_fields()`,
`stamp_complexity_provenance()`, the cache snapshot, and the knowledge
summary generator — then correctly-but-wrongly reports the substituted
values as founded, because the one bit of state that would have told them
otherwise was never carried across the cache-reuse copy.

### Affected code path

src/theforge/coordinator/preflight_cache.py:127-166 (apply_cached_preflight_state)
src/theforge/coordinator/state.py:715-733 (CoordinatorState preflight_degraded* field defaults)

### Fix-success criterion

Construct a source `CoordinatorState` with `preflight_degraded=True`,
`preflight_degraded_reason` set (e.g. `"parse_error"`), and
`preflight_failure_action`/`preflight_risk_signals` populated, along with a
valid `preflight_verdict`/`preflight_complexity_score`. Call
`apply_cached_preflight_state(state, cached_state)` on a fresh reusing
`CoordinatorState`. After the call, `state.preflight_degraded`,
`state.preflight_degraded_reason`, `state.preflight_failure_action`, and
`state.preflight_risk_signals` must equal the source state's values (not
the class defaults), and `complexity_source(state)` must return
`"preflight_degraded_conservative"` rather than `"preflight"`. An
integration-level check: a sprint run whose cached preflight source was
degraded must produce an audit record with `preflight.degraded: true` and
`preflight.complexity_source: preflight_degraded_conservative`, and the
corresponding knowledge summary must mark the story shape as
unfounded/degraded rather than presenting it as measured.

### Related findings (out of scope)

> These are adjacent problems noticed during investigation. They are **not** the cause of this issue's symptom and are **out of scope for this fix** — triage them separately under the linked issue. Do not implement them as part of this issue.

- _parse_preflight_verdict and its sibling _parse_preflight_* helpers in preflight.py all extract a fenced YAML block by finding the *next* triple-backtick after the opening fence, so response content that legitimately contains a fence (e.g. quoted source, quoted YAML) truncates or corrupts the parse — the same delimiter-matching defect issue #2216 already names for the diagnose flow, but present independently in the preflight extractors. (related: #2216)
- The preflight cache's source_run_id (e887dab00ac4) points to a run record that does not exist anywhere under .forge/audits/runs/, making the origin of a cached classification unrecoverable once that happens; worth checking whether batch-preflight sibling runs are ever fully persisted or are pruned/never-written for non-primary members of a batch.

### Notes

A related question the issue raises — "a cached classification whose
originating record is no longer available is itself a state the system
must be able to report" — is not resolved by this fix alone: even after
`apply_cached_preflight_state` correctly copies the degraded flag, the
cache's `source_run_id` (e887dab00ac4) pointing to a run with no file on
disk is a separate durability/retention gap outside this function. I did
not chase why that run record is missing (retention pruning? never
written for non-primary batch-preflight members?) — that is worth a
follow-up but is not necessary to confirm this issue's root cause, since
the field-copy omission reproduces the symptom regardless of whether the
source run record still exists on disk.

The issue's third expectation — "a parser recovering a structured response
from surrounding text must not let delimiter-like content inside the
response truncate it, and this applies to every extractor doing this kind
of recovery, not just the one most recently observed" — is the subject of
issue #2216 (nested-fence truncation in the diagnose flow) and is a
distinct defect in `_parse_preflight_verdict` and its sibling
`_parse_preflight_*` helpers in `preflight.py` (all of which use the same
naive `output.index("```", start)` "next fence closes the block" logic).
I have recorded this as a related finding rather than folding it into this
issue's confirmed_cause, since fixing the delimiter-matching logic is a
parser-robustness fix distinct from the state-copy omission this issue's
symptom is about — even a fully correct parse still needs the degraded
flag to survive caching for a genuine parse failure (of any cause) to be
reported correctly.

findings.description: When a preflight response is wrapped in a four-backtick YAML fence and contains an unindented triple-backtick snippet before later classification keys, the parser stops at the inner snippet and later keys such as work_type and domains fall back to defaults.

A preflight response wrapped in a four-backtick envelope so that it can quote an ordinary three-backtick snippet is cut off at that quoted snippet, so every classification field appearing after it is lost and the run records the substituted work type and empty domains with degraded false, as though the classifier had produced them.

The extractor's docstring states that a longer outer fence lets the body include ordinary triple-backtick snippets after the structured classification, while the code discards everything from the first inner snippet onward.

finding_registry.description: When a preflight response is wrapped in a four-backtick YAML fence and contains an unindented triple-backtick snippet before later classification keys, the parser stops at the inner snippet and later keys such as work_type and domains fall back to defaults.

The extractor's docstring states that a longer outer fence lets the body include ordinary triple-backtick snippets after the structured classification, while the code discards everything from the first inner snippet onward.
The change added a generated knowledge summary artifact under .forge for an unrelated run, so the patch now carries durable run data outside the normal source, test, and documentation trees.

Persisted knowledge summaries gained a provenance block on story_shape and a new top-level domains_provenance key while schema_version stayed at 1, so artifacts written before and after this change are indistinguishable by version even though their shapes differ.

The branch removes the persisted knowledge summary for run cf857907b6ed, an unrelated story's artifact that exists on the upstream default branch, so merging the branch deletes that run's story shape, domains, learned claims and review insights from the corpus that prior-run selection reads.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
